newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila banker says credit default fears overblown.
newsitem.headline: Manila banker says credit default fears overblown.

text.p: Fears over rising default in real estate and consumer loans are unfounded, Rafael Buenaventura, outgoing president of the Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) said on Thursday.
"The reports that are coming out are rather overblown, and tend to create a sense of gloom and doom," Buenaventura told reporters.
Buenaventura, who is president of Philippine Commercial International Bank, has finished his four-year term as BAP president and is holding the office until a new person is appointed.

Philippine banking shares have been severely battered in the past few days on reports that a survey by the Central Bank showed that bad loans, especially from home mortgages and auto loans, have been on the rise.
Many investors likened the situation to the recent Thai experience where finance firms were hit by lower revenues due to deteriorating loan portfolio quality.
Buenaventura said the sharp rise in the industry's loan portfolio was due to increased economic activity and higher consumer spending brought about a resurging economy in the past years.
The Thai banking industry has been piling up loans, especially in the form of mortgages, over the past 10 years, he said.
"You're comparing apples and oranges ... In the Philippines, the overbuilding is not there yet," he said.
A recent central bank report said banks' exposure to the property sector was about 10 percent of the total loan portfolio, which Buenaventura said was one of the lowest in the region.
He said, however, the Thai experience should give Philippine banks a due reminder to reassess aggressive lending strategies.
"We should look at the Thai experience really as an early warning signal," he added.
